title: ICU mortality prediction
summary: Candidate coordinates for developing or validating mortality prediction models in ICU data. The prediction time, target population, mortality horizon, validation design, calibration, and missing-data workflow must be declared before model fitting.

design_candidates.population: A clinically defined ICU target population with patient-level independence between development and validation data.
design_candidates.time_zero: The intended prediction time, commonly ICU admission or a prespecified later landmark.
design_candidates.observation_window: Only information available by the prediction time, with preprocessing and imputation learned inside training data.
design_candidates.prediction_or_followup_window: ICU, hospital, or fixed-horizon mortality defined consistently across datasets.
eligibility_candidates: Report missingness and outcome ascertainment by site
design_candidates.exposure: A prespecified predictor set available at the prediction landmark.
design_candidates.outcome: Mortality at a declared horizon with source, censoring, and transfer handling documented.
design_candidates.estimand: Individual predicted probability of mortality at the declared horizon in the target population.
recommended_methods: Calibration plot, slope, intercept, and discrimination

stop_conditions: Prediction time occurs after candidate predictors
Mortality horizon differs irreconcilably between development and validation data
Patient identifiers cannot prevent split leakage

citations.title: TRIPOD+AI statement: updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models
PROBAST: A Tool to Assess the Risk of Bias and Applicability of Prediction Model Studies
supports: participant, predictor, outcome, and analysis checks
